answer: Weight each identity's reward sublinearly: total influence from N agents scales as the square root of N, not N, while every identity still carries a fixed real onboarding cost c. A Sybil's gains then ripple outward with sharp diminishing returns, but its costs keep climbing linearly, opening a widening canyon between the two curves. Spinning up 1000 clones buys only about 31x one honest agent's reward (sqrt of 1000) yet pays 1000 times c; past the break-even horizon every extra fake is pure loss, so mass cloning never pays.
